items.title: Meloni si smarca. La scelta anti-tycoonper non perdere voti
items.summary: Ma Palazzo Chigi eviterà di cavalcare la difesa della Corte e proverà a giocare la carta della soluzione diplomatica
items.content:
ROMA – La riflessione, a Palazzo Chigi, è stata breve. Il confronto con la Farnesina ancora più rapido. Impossibile per l’Italia non partecipare alla dichiarazione congiunta con cui i membri del G7 (ad eccezione degli Stati Uniti) si sono schierati a favore della Corte penale internazionale e contro le sanzioni annunciate da Donald Trump. Impossibile restare al fianco di Washington – in questa battaglia spalleggiata da Israele – senza pagare un prezzo politico devastante. Un costo che la premier non intende affrontare, a pochi mesi dalle elezioni.

Non c’è stato dubbio, dunque. Per non rischiare di finire nel mirino delle opposizioni, fonti della Farnesina anticipano la pubblicazione dello statement e fanno sapere che Roma ha aderito alla condanna: meglio non tacere, perché potrebbe passare il messaggio che l’Italia si voglia schierare soltanto a causa delle critiche del centrosinistra. E così si spiega anche l’intervento di Antonio Tajani: «Il Nobel per la Pace è assegnato. È stata scelta una donna che ha una grande esperienza, è giusto che sia così. Non è che gli Usa devono commentare a chi si dà il premio».

Gli alleati europei erano stati preallertati dagli americani della mossa ostile alla Cpi. E avevano subito ragionato di come reagire. Prima della riunione dei ministri degli Esteri che licenzia il testo congiunto, Tajani ottiene l’ultimo via libera da Meloni. Inevitabile. E neanche particolarmente rischioso: lo scudo fornito dalle capitali europee e dagli altri partner del G7 rende la presa di posizione neanche troppo scomoda o scivolosa.

Arriva proprio nelle ore in cui Trump si presenta al Columbus day per ammiccare all’elettorato italo-americano con l’obiettivo di convincerlo a sostenerlo nelle elezioni di medio termine. Ma è una partita diversa, casi distinti che corrono su altri binari. E comunque, Palazzo Chigi eviterà di cavalcare la difesa della Cpi, a differenza di altri partner, anche perché con la Corte le relazioni restano fredde dopo il caso Al Masri. Semmai l’esecutivo batterà sulla necessità di provare a ricucire nel corso dei sei mesi che i contendenti hanno deciso di far trascorrere prima che le sanzioni entrino effettivamente in vigore .

La lettura di quanto accaduto tra Trump e la Cpi, invece, è univoca nelle diverse cancellerie continentali e occidentali. Ed è la stessa fornita informalmente dall’esecutivo italiano: una mossa ispirata da Benjamin Netanyahu, una sponda offerta dal tycoon all’amico in difficoltà in vista delle politiche in Israele.

Altre elezioni, quelle che in Italia si terranno nel 2027, orientano le mosse di Palazzo Chigi. Da molti mesi ormai – e certamente dopo gli insulti pubblici ricevuti da Trump – la presidente del Consiglio evita di mettere troppo la faccia sulle decisioni del Presidente Usa. Di difenderlo, di sostenerlo. Ha pagato un prezzo con l’opinione pubblica, non intende replicare. Certo, cerca di ripristinare relazioni civili. Ma per aiutarlo non intende rompere il fronte europeo, e men che meno mostrarsi conciliante con “Bibi”: non conviene e fa perdere voti, è la lezione ormai chiara al vertice del governo.

items.title: Commentator Katie Zacharia picked as new White House press secretary
items.summary: The conservative commentator currently works as a communications adviser at Trump Media & Technology Group.
items.content:
Donald Trump has chosen conservative commentator Katie Zacharia to be the next White House press secretary.

Zacharia, who currently works for Trump Media & Technology Group, will become the US president's sixth chief spokesperson across his two administrations. She previously had a brief stint as a spokeswoman at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

Trump called Zacharia "loyal" and "a devoted fan and member of MAGA" in a social media post on Friday, referring to his Make America Great Again movement, adding that she had "an unblemished record of support".

Former White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, who left the White House in August, has reportedly taken a job with Fox News.

"She was previously involved in my Campaigns, assisting in key Swing States, where we won 7 out of 7," Trump wrote on Truth Social of Zacharia.

"I am confident that Katie will deliver strong results for our Country as the next White House Press Secretary, as she has the respect of, and will work fantastically with, the Media, the American People, and my Administration."

Zacharia thanked him in a post on X, writing: "Serving President Trump and the American people at this critical 250-year mark is the honor of a lifetime."

She said Trump had "shown America that we can be great again, and he works to effectuate that greatness every single day".

She said she looked forward "to working with the White House press corps, and with reporters across the country, to get that record out".

The 42-year-old political strategist is a frequent fixture on conservative Newsmax and Fox News, and has been active in Republican politics for most of her adult life, having worked as an intern for the Republican National Committee and for the White House Office of Political Affairs during the Bush administration in 2006.

Since June, she has been a senior communications adviser for Trump's media company and Truth Social platform, according to her LinkedIn profile. She worked in Homeland Security from February to March this year.

While she was only briefly in government at DHS - which the mother of four later said she left because of the strain of travel between California and Washington on her family - she has long been a ferocious defender of President Trump and his administration's policies.

In a June interview with the BBC , for example, she dismissed criticism of Trump's controversial use of the White House to host a televised UFC fight, saying the principles of the UFC "are the kind of principles that founded our Constitutional Republic".

"It's about not giving up the fight until the bitter end," she said. "I think there's no better summation of the American ethos than a good UFC fight."

Earlier this year, Zacharia wrote an op-ed in the New York Post about an incident in which she was asked to stop wearing a "Make America Great Again" hat to her local gym.

"I responded that I would never take my Trump hat off to appease the left," she wrote. "This is raw, unfiltered intolerance. Freedom of speech doesn't evaporate at the gym door."

Justin Buchler, a political science professor at Case Western Reserve University in Ohio, told the BBC that Trump's appointments during his second term have been "based on personal affiliation and loyalty".

"He values loyalty first and foremost," Buchler told the BBC.

A lawyer educated at Pepperdine University in California, Zacharia also served as general counsel for Fix California, a conservative non-profit started by Trump ally - and current Special Presidential Envoy for Special Missions - Ric Grenell.

In 2011, she spent nearly two years clerking at a law firm in Beijing, China.

Trump says White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt to leave post

The complex job of press secretary goes beyond the briefing room podium to include managing contentious relationships with the press, coordinating with other parts of the White House, and providing media advice to the president. The secretary also oversees an office that receives a significant amount of inquiries and requests on a daily basis.

Yanna Krupnikov, a political scientist and professor of communication and media at the University of Michigan, said the selection of Zacharia "speaks to a blurring of the lines between different media types".

Politicians nowadays need to communicate not only to various news outlets but with people in a social media context, she said.

"I think the goal is not as much speaking to the media and journalists, but making sure that particular, very specific sound-bytes and messages get to ordinary people," Krupnikov told the BBC.

When Leavitt left the role, Trump called her one of his "most trusted aides", which sets a high bar for her replacement. Leavitt left because she said she wanted to spend more time with her family.

items.title: Terremoto di magnitudo 7.6 a Panama, gli Usa escludono il rischio tsunami
items.summary: Sospesa l'attività dell'aeroporto, chiuse le scuole. Scene di panico nella capitale. Al momento non si hanno notizie di vittime. Seconda scossa di magnitudo 6
items.content:
Un terremoto di magnitudo 7.6 è stato registrato nel sud di Panama , a 14 chilometri a sudovest di Pitaloza Arriba. Lo riporta l'istituto geologico statunitense Usgs. Il forte sisma ha provocato il panico nella capitale Panama City, riferiscono giornalisti Afp. Poco dopo c 'è stata una seconda scossa di terremoto di magnitudo 6. Lo comunica la rete panamense Rpc tv che sta già inviando le prime immagini di palazzi incrinati e calcinacci per strada, gente per strada dopo il forte terremoto che ha colpito lo stato centramericano. Al momento non si hanno notizie di vittime.

Le autorità stanno invitando la popolazione a non intasare le linee telefoniche e lasciare spazio ai soccorsi.

"Ho richiesto un rapporto ai ministri e agli enti competenti in merito agli effetti: si invita alla calma. Non c'è motivo di usare l'accaduto per generare allarme e disordine". Lo ha scritto su X il presidente di Panama Josè Mulino subito dopo il terremoto.

L'aeroporto internazionale di Panama h a comunicato di aver sospeso le attività per motivi precauzionali e per poter controllare le strutture. Inoltre sono state chiuse le scuole . Nelle zone più colpite di Coclè, Verguas e Azuero i vigili del fuoco stanno cominciando a verificare la tenuta degli edifici. I media locali trasmettono scene di persone che scappano nel panico dalle loro case e dai centri commerciali evacuati, dopo le scosse.

Il sistema di monitoraggio tsunami degli Stati Uniti ha diramato un'allerta per potenziale minaccia tsunami per diversi Paesi che si affacciano sul Pacifico orientale, dopo il sisma che ha colpito Panama. La segnalazione di possibile minaccia riguarda Ecuador, Colombia, Nicaragua, Panama, Guatemala, Messico, Perù, El Salvador, Costa Rica.

Lo 'U.S. Tsunami Warning System' ha poi ritirato l'allerta tsunami sulle coste centroamericane del Pacifico dopo aver pubblicato un primo avvertimento a seguito del terremoto di magnitudo 7,6. U na minaccia moderata di tsunami viene considerata invece dalle autorità di El Salvador mentre il rischio dell'arrivo di un'onda anomala viene scartato dall'Unità nazionale del rischio disastri della Colombia (Ungrd).

items.title: Japan's Most Famous Tuna Buyer Says He Turned Somali Pirates into Fishermen
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.japaninsides.com/the-sushi-king-who-went-to-somalia-how-japans-most-famous-tuna-buyer-says-he-turned-pirates-into-fishermen-55344 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50027167 Points: 22 # Comments: 6
items.content:
At the height of the Somali piracy crisis, with twenty navies patrolling the coast, a Tokyo restaurant owner flew in with four fishing boats and a promise to buy whatever they caught. The attacks collapsed. Who deserves the credit is still argued.

They were operating hundreds of miles out into the Indian Ocean from motherships, boarding tankers and bulk carriers with ladders and rifles, and sailing them back to anchor off the Somali coast. At any given time they were holding several hundred sailors hostage, sometimes for years, waiting for ransoms that ran into the millions.

Most of the world knew the problem from one incident two years earlier: the April 2009 hijacking of the Maersk Alabama and the capture of its American captain, Richard Phillips, which ended with Navy SEAL snipers firing from the fantail of a destroyer and became a Tom Hanks film.

By 2011, the response was enormous. Warships from the United States, the European Union, NATO, China, India, Russia, Japan and others were running patrols through the Gulf of Aden. Shipping companies had begun putting armed guards aboard. Ships were hardened with razor wire and citadels.

None of it had stopped the attacks. The year before, Somali pirates had taken more hostages than in any year on record.

He was, and is, the owner of Kiyomura Corporation, which runs the Sushi Zanmai chain across Japan. In Tokyo he is known as the Tuna King, because every January he buys the most expensive fish at the first auction of the year at the central market, pays a price that makes the front page of every newspaper, and sells it in his restaurants at the normal menu price. In January 2026 he paid 510 million yen - about $3.2 million - for a single bluefin from Oma, a world record.

Tuna is his business. And tuna is the reason he says he went to Somalia.

The waters off the Somali coast are some of the richest yellowfin grounds in the Indian Ocean. For two decades, with no functioning government to police them, foreign trawlers had been fishing them out. Somali fishermen, who had once worked those waters from small boats, had been pushed off their own coast.

Many of them, by the accounts that emerged in those years, were the men now doing the hijacking.

Kimura has told the story in Japanese interviews, and the details come from those.

Around 2012, he went to the Somali coast and met with men who had been involved in piracy. He says he wanted to understand why they were doing it.

His conclusion was that they didn’t want to be pirates. They wanted to feed their families, and the fishing had collapsed.

He says he provided four fishing boats. He taught the crews to catch yellowfin tuna. He set up freezer capacity on shore so the fish would keep until it could be shipped. He helped Somalia engage with the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission, the body that manages the fishery. And he committed to buying what they caught, at a stable price, so that a tuna was worth money the day it came out of the water.

By 2015, successful Somali hijackings had stopped altogether. The anchorages off the coast where hijacked ships had sat for years were empty.

The International Maritime Bureau, which compiles the figures, has a clear view of why. In its words, the decline came from “international navies, the hardening of vessels and other recommendations in the shipping industry’s Best Management Practices, the use of private armed security teams and the stabilizing influence of Somalia’s central government.”

Kimura’s name is not on that list. It does not appear in any naval or maritime-industry account of how the crisis ended.

What his program did is not something anyone outside his own interviews has measured. Four boats on one stretch of coast is not a national fishing industry. The men who stopped hijacking ships in 2012 did so, overwhelmingly, because boarding a ship had become a good way to get shot or spend life in a Seychelles prison.

But the pirates’ own explanation for why they started - foreign fleets took our fish, so we took their ships - was never really contested. And the one person who showed up offering to buy fish instead of sending a frigate was a sushi restaurant owner from Tokyo.

He has never claimed to have done it alone. The internet has claimed it for him, repeatedly, usually in the form “a Japanese sushi chef ended Somali piracy,” which is not true and which he has not said.

There is a version of Kimura that Japan knows well: the man in the white coat and the enormous grin, standing over a record-price bluefin with a cleaver every January, having just spent a fortune on a fish he will sell at a loss. It is a publicity stunt, and it is a very good one.

The Somalia story is the other version of the same man. The instinct is identical - if you want the fish, go where the fish are and pay for them - and so is the self-promotion. He tells the story because it is good for business.

Both things can be true. The publicity stunt that puts his face on every front page in Japan is also, by any reasonable accounting, the most expensive advertisement in the country. And the fishing program that he describes in Somalia, whatever its real scale, was a sushi man’s answer to a problem the navies of the world had spent four years failing to solve by force.

So it is a footnote, or it is the part everyone else missed. The numbers say navies. Kimura says tuna. It was probably both, in some proportion that nobody is ever going to measure - and the only person who went ashore to try the second one was the Tuna King.

items.title: Three men found guilty of murdering two Australian surfer brothers and US friend
items.summary: The bodies of Jake and Callum Robinson and their friend Carter Rhoad were found at the bottom of a well.
items.content:
Three men have been found guilty of murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, and their US friend Carter Rhoad during a surfing trip in Mexico in 2024.

The men's full names could not be given for legal reasons, and they were only identified as Jesús Gerardo, Irineo Francisco and Ángel Jesús. They are yet to be sentenced - but are likely to spend the rest of their lives in a prison.

Debra Robinson, the brother's mother, told the courtroom in the northern Baja California state the murders of her sons had taken "the future we had imagined with them".

During the trial the court heard the tourists were killed in an apparent botched robbery of their truck in a secluded beach area.

Their bodies were later found with gunshot wounds to their heads, dumped down a well.

The murders sent shockwaves around the world, particularly in Australia, as the coastal area is usually safe from the violence in other parts of Mexico.

Debra Robinson and her husband Martin Robinson have been at the court in the coastal town of Ensenada throughout the trial and they delivered emotional testimony during closing arguments before Friday's verdict.

"It's hard for a parent to lose a son, and we lost two sons," said Martin.

Speaking to media outside court a week ago, Debra Robinson said the couple were "deeply grateful" to Australians for the outpouring of support they had received and that they "feel the love and their arms around us".

During the month-long trial, the prosecution had sought 150 years in prison for each of the three defendants.

In November last year, the girlfriend of the alleged ringleader, Jesús Gerardo alias "El Kekas", was sentenced in a separate trial to 20 years in prison. She had admitted to involvement in the robbery.

At the time, the murders shocked locals and tourists in Ensenada who were disturbed at the apparent ease and sheer pointlessness of the killings.

The beach town has a reputation as a welcoming spot for surfers and the chilling murders revealed much about how commonplace such extreme violence remains in Mexico.

The only explanation the authorities appeared able to give was that the surfers - all in their early 30s - had ultimately been murdered for being in the wrong place at the wrong time.

Their killings took place barely 36 hours after they crossed into Mexico from the US. Their bodies, however, were not found for another week when their families were able to identify them.

At the time, the surfer community in Ensenada turned out in force to commemorate the men by paddling out at one of the area's best known surfing spots and throwing flowers into the sea.

Local surfers also called for greater security for residents and visiting tourists, citing other recent examples of violence in the state. Tourism is a key part of the regional economy in Baja California.

Amid the demands for action, Baja California Governor Marina del Pilar Ávila tried to ease public fears about the widespread violence in her state.

"Baja California is and will continue to be a state with safe tourism for the thousands of people who visit us from the rest of the country and the world", she said.

"I send my condolences and solidarity to the families at this difficult time."

items.title: Trump: 'Con Meloni c'è un grande rapporto' e incassa l'accordo con Putin sul diesel
items.summary: La Casa Bianca sospende le sanzioni fino ad aprile. Il tycoon: 'Ribassi record dei prezzi'. Putin conferma l'accordo: 'Avrà un impatto positivo sull'intera economia globale'
items.content:
"Ho un grande rapporto con lei. Andiamo d'accordo". Lo ha detto il presidente Donald Trump rispondendo a chi gli chiedeva quali fossero i rapporti con la premier Giorgia Meloni. Alla domanda se intendesse incontrarla al G20, Trump ha detto: "Probabilmente".

Trump si assicura il diesel da Putin. Zelensky, 'lo pagherà con altro terrore' (di Alberto Zanconato)

Gli Usa provano a rilanciare le trattative per mettere fine al conflitto in Ucraina, con una delegazione di Kiev e inviati europei che arrivano a Miami per colloqui di due giorni con i negoziatori statunitensi Steve Witkoff e Jared Kushner. Ma contemporaneamente Donald Trump apre una partita su un altro tavolo, parlando al telefono con Vladimir Putin e assicurandosi da lui un aiuto prezioso in vista delle elezioni di Midterm: forniture di milioni di tonnellate di gasolio, che saranno esentate dalle sanzioni Usa fino ad aprile, nell'intento di abbassare i prezzi dell'energia.

Un annuncio confermato dallo stesso Putin, dicendosi "fiducioso che ciò avrà un impatto positivo sull'intera economia globale". Immediata la reazione di Volodymyr Zelensky: "Regali a Putin non porteranno pace né alcun beneficio al mondo civile e la Russia 'ripagherà' il diesel con ulteriore terrore e perfidia", ha scritto su X, mentre fonti di Kiev hanno riferito ad Axios la "sorpresa" del governo ucraino di fronte all'annuncio di Trump.

"Permettere alla Russia di vendere prodotti petroliferi - ha aggiunto il presidente ucraino - è un investimento in una guerra che deve essere terminata, non prolungata. Ciò che serve è una vera de-escalation con la Russia su base reciproca". Ma, sul suo social Truth, Trump ha usato toni trionfalistici nell'annunciare l'accordo. "Ho appena concluso un colloquio di grande successo con il presidente russo Vladimir Putin", ha scritto il presidente Usa. "E' stato concordato - ha spiegato Trump - che la Russia fornirà immediatamente oltre 300.000 tonnellate di gasolio al mercato americano e globale, altre 500.000 tonnellate nel mese di novembre e 1.000.000 di tonnellate subito dopo. Inoltre, in base alla capacità delle loro raffinerie, la Russia consegnerà, in tempi brevi, ulteriori 3.000.000 di tonnellate di gasolio".

Insomma, "grazie al nostro controllo dello Stretto di Hormuz e a questo importante annuncio sull'energia russa, i prezzi del gasolio per gli americani e per il mondo intero caleranno rapidamente e in misura record", ha aggiunto il tycoon, facendo capire di essersi in qualche modo assicurato il voto di Putin nella delicata scadenza elettorale che lo attende il mese prossimo.

Proprio uno degli argomenti in discussione a Miami, secondo fonti americane citate dall'Afp. E, in contemporanea con l'annuncio di Trump, il ministero del Tesoro ha fatto sapere di avere concesso una sospensione delle sanzioni Usa sulla fornitura di gasolio russo ai mercati mondiali per i prossimi sei mesi. Intanto Witkoff e Kushner, che il mese scorso si erano recati a Mosca e a Kiev, ricevono in Florida la delegazione ucraina, guidata dal capo dell'ufficio presidenziale Kyrylo Budanov e quello dell'intelligence, Rustem Umerov, oltre ai consiglieri per la sicurezza nazionale di Gran Bretagna, Francia e Germania, insieme a rappresentanti della Nato e dell'Unione europea.

L'iniziativa di Washington fa seguito alle dichiarazioni di giovedì del segretario di Stato Marco Rubio secondo cui le ostilità hanno raggiunto livelli potenzialmente esplosivi, con il pericolo di una seria escalation. "Non pensiamo che ci sia una soluzione militare al conflitto", aveva sottolineato il capo della diplomazia Usa. Kiev, inoltre, si appresta ad affrontare un altro inverno che si prospetta come il più duro dall'inizio della guerra, dopo essere stata martellata per settimane dai missili e dai droni russi che hanno preso di mira infrastrutture, centri logistici, industrie e porti sul Mar Nero.

I raid, ha sottolineato il presidente Volodymyr Zelensky, hanno provocato "danni considerevoli" alla rete elettrica nazionale e "i lavori di ripristino proseguono giorno e notte". Mosca si è sempre dichiarata contraria a tregue settoriali e temporanee, dicendo di volere arrivare a un trattato di pace che preveda "una soluzione per le generazioni future", come ha affermato ancora giovedì il portavoce del Cremlino, Dmitry Peskov. Ma ora, forse, la revoca almeno temporanea delle sanzioni americane potrebbe facilitare un parziale cessate il fuoco nei bombardamenti.

items.title: Trump announces deal for Russian diesel as Zelensky criticises 'gift to Putin'
items.summary: Ukraine's president said allowing Russia to sell petroleum products would prolong a war that must be ended.
items.content:
US President Donald Trump says he has reached an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin allowing Moscow to "immediately release" diesel to the US and globally.

Trump said the proposed release of hundreds of thousands of tonnes of Russian diesel, in tranches, would see prices "COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!".

It is understood the US Treasury is suspending sanctions on Russian diesel exports until 7 April 2027 as part of the deal, but other assets like those in American banks are still frozen.

Ukraine's president criticised the decision, saying any easing of sanctions on Russia played into Moscow's hands and would prolong the war between the two countries.

Trump said Putin had agreed to release 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and another million after that.

He added that a further three million tonnes of Russian diesel would be delivered "within a short period" after, dependent on the condition of its refineries, which have seen attacks by Ukraine.

Putin later said Russia was willing to supply both the US and global markets with oil and petroleum products, but his statement did not specify amounts.

The BBC has asked the White House for clarity on what Russia will get from the US in return for the commitment.

Friday's announcement is the latest effort from Trump to lower fuel prices in the US, as he has spent months grappling with the political consequences of the Iran war, which began in February, and its impact on global energy prices.

That conflict has sent the cost of petrol and, in particular diesel, skyrocketing in America in recent months, which has soured his standing with the public who have been stung by the higher pump prices and knock-on effects that led to across-the board inflation.

The average diesel price in the US is currently $6.28 (£4.74) a gallon, according to the AAA, down from the record high of $6.53 recorded at the end of September.

Shortly after Trump's announcement, the US Treasury formally issued a temporary licence allowing Russian diesel into the market.

Putin said in a statement that he had spoken to Trump about the global energy situation on Friday, adding: "The Russian side confirmed its willingness to supply oil and petroleum products to the US market and global markets at large."

An envoy for Putin, Kirill Dmitriev, welcomed the deal on social media, saying: "Russia-US co-operation on diesel and energy will benefit the world."

But Zelensky hit out at it, saying "gifts to Putin will not work for peace" and that Russia would repay the diesel with "further terror".

"Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged," he wrote on social media.

Russia has this year experienced two waves of severe fuel shortages across the country as a result of Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries, and introduced a ban on diesel exports.

According to the International Energy Agency, its diesel production is estimated to have fallen by nearly 30%.

Trump has expressed his displeasure over those attacks, blaming them for rising fuel prices.

But Zelensky defended the strikes on Friday, saying there were in response to "Russia's years-long campaign of terror against Ukraine's energy sector".

"Ukraine will not set Russian oil refineries on fire if Russia does not destroy our energy infrastructure," he said.

Trump wants to reduce the cost of fuel as the midterms loom - will it work?

Trump's Truth Social posts often provide incomplete information and the details of exactly how Russia is supplying this fuel to the global market, and what they might get for in return is unclear.

But the announced deal represents a remarkable about-face, as the US Congress recently enacted legislation - signed by the president - to authorise new American sanctions and tariffs on nations that import Russian oil and gas.

The agreement with Russia also opens Trump up to criticism from European allies and pro-Ukraine politicians in the US, that the American president is now helping to fund Moscow's war machine.

What impact the deal with Russia will have on fuel prices also remains unclear. The global benchmark for crude oil, Brent, remains above $103 a barrel. Before the war with Iran, Brent crude was trading at about $73 a barrel.

With the looming US midterm congressional elections - which will determine if Republicans maintain control of Congress - Trump has been searching for ways to ease his Republican party's political pain.

Earlier this week, he said he was "thinking about" suspending the federal tax on gasoline and also announced that he would allow so-called red dye diesel to be used on US highways without facing federal tax.

Trump has also successfully pressured G7 nations into releasing 100 million barrels of oil and diesel from stockpiles to help ease supply concerns, and previously supported calls for a ban on diesel exports from the US.

items.title: JD Vance casts doubt on firing squad execution and says he will not watch it
items.summary: The planned execution of Nidal Hasan by firing squad would be the first military execution in more than 60 years.
items.content:
US Vice-President JD Vance has cast doubt on the Pentagon's plans to livestream a firing squad execution of the Fort Hood shooter.

Talking with reporters, Vance expressed doubt that the December execution would go forward as planned, saying: "I don't know that that's actually going to happen". He added, that "if it's through live stream, I'm not going to be watching it".

Hours later, US President Donald Trump said he "absolutely" approved the live stream plans but said the Pentagon was still "making a determination" on it.

Hasan killed 13 unarmed US soldiers at a base in Texas in 2009, injuring another 32. The firing squad execution would be the first military execution in more than 60 years.

The Pentagon announced earlier this week it would execute former US Army major Nidal Hasan on 3 December 2026 by firing squad in the attack on the Fort Hood base.

Then on Thursday US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said the execution would be livestreamed for the public. "People need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things," Hegseth explained.

Trump, as he left the White House on Friday, was asked about the possibility that visuals of Hasan's execution could be used as propaganda for terrorists.

"He killed 13, 14 people, badly wounded 20-some-odd people, and he's totally nuts," Trump said. "So I really don't care how he goes, as long as he goes, and I think that the death penalty is a very worthy way of going for him."

The BBC has contacted the Pentagon for more information about the livestream determination.

Speaking to reporters on Friday, Vance condemned Hasan's attack on the base as "the worst terrorist attack on American soil outside of 9/11". Asked about how his Catholic faith impacted his stance on plans to stream a public execution, Vance cast doubt on whether they would happen.

But he noted that Hasan, who was a US Army psychiatrist, was meant to treat soldiers for mental illness and other problems and "took them at their most vulnerable and gunned down these people where they lived".

The announcement of the livestream plans has been met with criticism from both political parties.

Republican Senator John Curtis pointed to Rome's history of a "bloody spectacle" corrupting people who watched them, warning that public executions erode civilisations "when it cultivates an appetite for executions as a form of entertainment".

Curtis said that Hegseth's plan "risks feeding that appetite" and urged him to reconsider.

"The victims deserve justice administered with solemnity. Broadcasting a death diminishes us and is not an effective deterrent," he said.

Democratic Senator Chris Murphy told CNN that the idea was "disgusting" and reminiscent of executions carried out by the Islamic State group.

Georgia lawmaker Austin Scott, a Republican, said that he "absolutely" supports the death sentence, but that live-streaming executions "is what jihadists do. America is better than that".

The US Conference of Catholic Bishops condemned the decision to publicly livestream Hasan's execution, expressing "shock and great sorrow" in a statement.

The UN human rights office told AFP that livestreaming it would be "tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture".

Hasan opened fire in a crowded medical building where deploying soldiers were awaiting check-ups and vaccines.

He later admitted in court that he was the gunman and apologised for "any mistakes". He said during his court-martial in 2013 that he believed he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan from the US military.

The killings on 5 November 2009 were the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American military base.

Military law requires that military execution be approved by the US president. It also requires appellate review, when a higher court inspects the decision and gives a final judgement on its legality to move forward.

While there were more than 2,700 executions across 17 countries last year, only two nations carried them out publicly. Eleven public executions were known to have been carried out in Iran in 2025 and another six in Afghanistan, according to Amnesty International.

Fort Hood survivor supports gunman's execution by firing squad but questions livestream

When Hegseth told reporters on Thursday about plans to ensure the public can watch the execution, he did not specify where or how live video of the execution would be shown.

A Pentagon spokesperson on Friday reiterated to the BBC that Hasan's execution "will be livestreamed," but said the government had no further details "to provide at this time".

The White House did not respond to an inquiry about whether it expected to show Hasan's planned execution on its social media channels.

The White House maintains official accounts and channels on the most notable and widely used online platforms that are capable of streaming live video, namely Meta, YouTube, TikTok and X.

All of the platforms have prohibitions in place on violent images and videos, as well as those that show death or glorify or make a spectacle of violence.

Meta, owner of Instagram, Facebook and Threads, explicitly bans any live stream of capital punishment.

YouTube bans all "violent or gory content intended to shock or disgust viewers".

TikTok has a similar rule that bars "extremely graphic, violent, or disturbing content—especially when it could cause viewers emotional distress." That includes the "moment of someone's death" and "the shooting of an individual".

Both YouTube and TikTok make exceptions in instances of "public interest".

Asked if a live-stream of an execution qualifies for the exception if it is government-sanctioned , a TikTok spokeswoman said: "Regardless, I'd point you back to the not allowed section which reflects our approach."

The policy at X, which has loosened content moderation since billionaire Elon Musk took over the platform, prohibits content "glorifying" of violence. It will remove content depicting when a person dies will be removed if requested by certain parties.

Meta, YouTube and X did not respond to multiple BBC requests for comment on whether they would uphold their current policies in the event Hasan's execution is broadcast.

Fort Hood attacker to be executed by firing squad - a first for US military since World War Two

Christa Pike now walking after failed US execution, lawyer tells BBC

items.title: Powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake hits Panama, damaging buildings
items.summary: Tsunami warnings are issued for neighbouring countries as videos of destruction circulate online.
items.content:
A massive magnitude 7.7 earthquake has hit Panama, damaging buildings and causing widespread shaking.

About 4.6 million people felt moderate to severe tremors as a result of the quake, according to the US Geological Survey, which has said that the effects of the quake were "likely to be widespread".

It struck just before 15:00 local time (18:00 GMT) on Friday, with an epicentre about 6.2 miles (10km) from the town of Pitaloza Arriba in south-central Panama.

Footage shared online appears to show collapsed buildings in the towns of Penonomé and Soná, including one of a man calling out to anyone trapped under the rubble of a collapsed building. No casualties have so far been reported.

Verified footage shows one side of a cathedral in Penonomé collapsed due to the shaking, as well as one of its spires.

Another video showed a local hotel had almost completely collapsed.

Ricardo Brown, who lives in the southern Herrera province, told news agency Reuters that the earthquake had damaged several homes in his neighbourhood of Las Minas.

"We're scared. It's just the two of us old folks here. The house has cracked and we're afraid it could fall on us," the 74-year-old said.

The full extent of the damage it has caused is not yet clear, though several large aftershocks were also reported near the initial earthquake, potentially complicating the situation on the surface.

The quake was registered as occurring at a depth of just 12km. The shallower the earthquake, the more likely it is to have more severe effects on the surface.

Many people were evacuated from buildings in Panama City, about 200km from the epicentre, and were seen taking to the streets or sitting in nearby parks until the shaking had ceased.

Damage in the capital appears to be limited to that caused by debris falling from roofs.

Panama's President José Raúl Mulino said his entire government was mobilising in response to the earthquake, adding: "What happened should not be used to cause alarm or disorder."

Tsunami warnings were initially issued for 11 countries neighbouring Panama, before the US Tsunami Warning System confirmed there was no threat.

The Panama Canal - a vital waterway linking the Atlantic and Pacific oceans - was unaffected by the earthquake, the authority that oversees marine traffic through it said.

The earthquake comes just three days before Panama was scheduled to hold a national evacuation drill for dealing with a major earthquake.

It also follows devastating earthquakes in Colombia and Venezuela earlier this year.

items.title: OpenAI mistranslated mathematics into code for its Navier-Stokes proof
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.newscientist.com/article/2592824-openai-mistranslated-mathematics-into-code-for-its-navier-stokes-proof/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50026734 Points: 26 # Comments: 2
items.content:
OpenAI appears to have made a subtle error when publishing its proofs of the Navier-Stokes problem, a team of mathematicians has claimed. The error doesn’t mean that the proofs are incorrect or that OpenAI hasn’t correctly solved the problem, but it does call into question whether mathematical results generated by AI models can always be relied on.

“What has to be done with all of these large language model-generated proofs is that they will have to be read by humans, and this creates an enormous extra burden on mathematicians,” says Anders Hansen at the University of Cambridge.

On 8 September, OpenAI announced that it had found a solution to the Navier-Stokes problem , one of the most famous open problems in mathematics. It published the proof in two versions – one written in “natural language”, meaning a combination of English and mathematical symbols, as a human mathematician would write, and another written in the computer code Lean. The Lean proof is meant to be a formalisation of the natural-language version, allowing a computer to mechanically verify that all of its logical statements are true. The problem is, say Hansen and his team, that they don’t match.

“This formalisation process is trying to replace peer review,” says team member Fabian Circelli , also at the University of Cambridge. “Peer review would mean that human eyes look at the proofs. But what we’ve shown in this paper is that using this type of AI auto-formalisation can’t serve the same purpose.”

The most interesting mathematical discoveries in OpenAI’s 722 new papers

To be clear, the researchers aren’t saying that OpenAI has failed to solve the Navier-Stokes problem. It is entirely possible that both the natural-language proof and the Lean one provide a solution, just as there are hundreds of valid proofs of Pythagoras’s theorem . Instead, their point is a more subtle one: that OpenAI’s model has “mistranslated” when converting into Lean.

“We are not saying that the natural-language proof is wrong,” says Hansen. “Nor do we say that it is correct.” The issue is that OpenAI presents the two proofs as identical, stating on Github that “This repository contains Lean 4 formalizations of the results presented in [the paper] ‘Finite time blowup for Navier–Stokes’”.

This mistranslation occurs because the AI has to produce a Lean proof that “compiles”, meaning that the computer code is fully self-consistent and doesn’t produce an error, says Hansen. If, in the process of auto-formalisation, the AI finds a section of the proof that doesn’t compile, it will attempt to find a workaround even if it means diverging from the proof as written in natural language.

OpenAI has dumped 722 maths papers – now it must clean up the mess

The team’s specific claim hinges on part of the proofs called Lemma 8.6. In the natural-language proof, an equation in this part requires that a certain value be below m + 4, where m is a whole number. In the Lean proof, the equivalent value is required to be below m + 5, which is mathematically weaker.

To understand why, imagine being asked to solve the equation x + 3 = 6, to which the answer is x = 3. It is possible to write a proof that x must be less than 4, and also that x must be less than 5. Both of these are perfectly true mathematical statements, but they say different things. The latter proof allows more possible answers for x , making it mathematically weaker.

OpenAI told New Scientist that it is aware of the mismatch between the natural-language proof and the Lean code, and that this doesn’t mean that either proof is invalid. It says it will rectify any errors in the natural-language proof as they are found, and will also continue the process of formalising the 722 maths papers the firm released this week , only some of which are accompanied by Lean proofs, which themselves haven’t been checked by hand.

Finding the divergence involved a slightly surreal process of asking ChatGPT to look for potential discrepancies between the natural-language and Lean proofs, then checking them by hand. Many of the discrepancies suggested by ChatGPT turned out, on inspection, to be consistent after all. “Going through all of these things manually was a nightmare,” says Hansen.

In all, it took the team about two weeks to identify a true discrepancy, compared with the 88 hours OpenAI said its agents spent generating the proofs. “OpenAI boast about how quickly they were able to generate this result, but that’s only part of the process,” says team member Alexander Bastounis at King’s College London.

Answering the question of whether AI models can accurately auto-formalise mathematics is essential if mathematicians are to trust these results. Anders and his team have demonstrated that it is possible for ChatGPT to produce a Lean version of a proof that doesn’t match the original natural language one, with the AI silently altering the logical argument in the process to cover up any errors. “It is trying to help me, but by doing that, it is not helping,” says Hansen.

If this were to happen for a long and complicated proof, it would be very difficult for anyone to notice without inspecting both versions in detail. This issue is only more pressing because of the batch of 722 papers OpenAI just released. If we think ‘all of this is now true, the only thing we need to do now is read the paper’, then that is dangerous, says Hansen. “The purpose of doing science is that mankind should have an understanding of how the world works so we can make educated decisions. If we lose that understanding, what are doing?”

Kevin Buzzard at Imperial College London notes that in discussions like these, it is important to distinguish between the statement of a theorem and its proof. For example, the statement of the famous Fermat’s last theorem is that for positive whole number a , b , c and n , aⁿ + bⁿ = cⁿ only if n is 1 or 2. This is easy to convert into Lean and can easily be checked. Once you are happy that a statement in Lean is correct, if the proof of that statement compiles, you can be confident the proof is true.

The issue, as Hansen and his team have pointed out, is that this tells you nothing about the natural-language version of a proof published as a PDF document. “I am confident that the Navier-Stokes problem has been correctly resolved,” says Buzzard. “I am far less confident that the proof described in the PDF is correct.”

Hansen says he hopes OpenAI will take the team’s work “very seriously” and that more work must be done on developing robust auto-formalisation techniques. “Do we have the solution? Not yet. Is it possible to do this in a controlled way? Yes, it will be, but the optimal and the ultimate way of doing this is completely unknown.”

items.title: Perù, Hitler Mussolini Simeón eletto sindaco a Queropalca
items.summary: Clamore mediatico per il nome del candidato vincitore
items.content:
Nelle recenti elezioni regionali e municipali in Perù, un candidato ha attirato l'attenzione generale per la particolarità del suo nome. Hitler Mussolini Simeón Flores, esponente del partito Ahora Nación, è il vincitore virtuale per la carica di sindaco nel distretto di Queropalca, situato nella provincia di Lauricocha. La sua affermazione elettorale ha suscitato clamore mediatico per l'evidente coincidenza anagrafica con il leader del regime nazista e con il dittatore italiano fondatore del fascismo.

Il nuovo primo cittadino ha conquistato la vittoria ottenendo 229 preferenze, pari al 34,54% dei voti validi. La competizione elettorale distrettuale è stata serratissima e si è decisa per un margine minimo, con una differenza di appena 42 schede tra la prima e la terza posizione in classifica.

Al secondo posto si è infatti piazzato il partito Renovación Popular Perú con 204 voti (30,76%), seguito a stretto giro da País para Todos con 187 consensi. Molto più distaccati gli altri sfidanti, tra cui Alianza para el Progreso e Somos Perú (fermo a otto voti), in uno scrutinio che ha registrato un totale di 663 voti validi.

items.title: La fucilazione del killer di Fort Hood in diretta streaming, per l'Onu è tortura
items.summary: Sdegno per l'annuncio shock di Hegseth. I vescovi Usa: 'Barbarie'. Trump: 'Se lo merita'
items.content:
La fucilazione di Nidal Hasan, l'ex maggiore dell'esercito che nel 2009 uccise 13 persone e ne ferì altre 32 in una violenta sparatoria alla base militare di Fort Hood, in Texas, sarà trasmessa in diretta streaming. "Una violazione al divieto assoluto di tortura", ha tuonato l'Ufficio dell'Alto Commissario per i diritti umani dell'Onu, unendosi allo sdegno per l'annuncio shock del capo del Pentagono.

"La gente deve capire che ci sono gravi conseguenze per questo tipo di azioni", ha sostenuto Pete Hegseth, parlando dell'esecuzione già programmata per il prossimo 3 dicembre, proprio nel luogo dell'attacco di Fort Hood, a un orario (le 13:00) tale da coincidere con l'inizio della sparatoria. "Se la merita la pena di morte per fucilazione", ha rincarato il presidente Donald Trump, che in settimana aveva autorizzato il plotone di esecuzione che per i militari non veniva schierato dalla fine della Seconda guerra mondiale.

"Non so se accadrà davvero. Quest'uomo ha compiuto il peggior attentato terroristico sul suolo americano dopo l'11 Settembre. Se alla fine dovesse essere trasmesso in diretta streaming, io non la guarderò", ha commentato il vicepresidente Usa, JD Vance, replicando in Ohio a una domanda su come sia possibile conciliare la sua fede cristiana alla controversa vicenda.

L'inedita mossa del Pentagono ha creato un forte fronte critico bipartisan anche in Congresso. "Hasan deve affrontare la pena capitale, ma rendere pubblica la sua esecuzione e trasmetterla in streaming? È assolutamente ripugnante", ha scritto il senatore Thom Tillis, repubblicano della Carolina del Nord, in un post su X. "Le esecuzioni pubbliche sono pratiche tipiche di dittature oppressive come l'Iran e l'Afghanistan. Non dovrebbero accadere in America", ha rincarato Tillis.

Simili i commenti del senatore dem Chris Murphy: l'idea è "ripugnante" e ricorda le esecuzioni compiute dall'Isis. Il paradosso della decisione di Trump è che le forze armate americane non utilizzano questo metodo dal 1945 e non dispongono più di una procedura moderna per attuarlo.

Nel caso di Hasan pesano anche altre considerazioni sia sul suo trasferimento da Fort Leavenworth, in Kansas, sia sulle sue condizioni, dato che è paralizzato ed è costretto su una sedia a rotelle dopo le ferite riportate nella sparatoria. La scelta della fucilazione ha costretto quindi l'esercito Usa ad abbandonare mesi di pianificazione basati su modalità diverse. Documenti interni hanno chiarito che i funzionari si stavano preparando a ricorrere alle iniezioni letali. Le stesse della recente e incredibile vicenda di Christa Pike, in Tennessee, sopravvissuta a due tentativi.

Intanto, Jamaal Howard, un americano di 46 anni, è stato giustiziato in Texas tramite una iniezione letale, in quella che è la prima esecuzione dopo il tentativo più volte fallito contro Christa Pike in Tennessee, appena una settimana prima. Quella di Howard, condannato a morte per aver ucciso un addetto alle vendite durante una rapina nel 2000, è la trentesima pena capitale eseguita negli Stati Uniti nel 2026.

L'uomo è stato dichiarato morto dopo la somministrazione di una dose letale di pentobarbital nel penitenziario statale di Huntsville. Quando il direttore del carcere gli ha chiesto se avesse un'ultima dichiarazione da rilasciare, Howard ha chiesto scusa ad alcuni familiari della vittima, che assistevano all'esecuzione attraverso una vetrata a pochi metri dalla camera della morte. "Spero che accettiate le mie scuse e spero nel vostro perdono", ha detto poco prima che cominciassero le operazioni dell'iniezione letale. "Mi dispiace per quanto accaduto. Spero che un giorno possiate imparare a perdonarmi", ha aggiunto, ringraziando amici e familiari e dicendo di amarli. Ha detto anche di essere "sereno e pronto a trovare la pace e il Signore; vi ringrazio tutti". Ha concluso dicendo: "Godetevi la vita e pace a voi tutti".

items.title: No Man Is an Island
items.summary: Article URL: https://borretti.me/article/no-man-is-an-island Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50025935 Points: 247 # Comments: 145
items.content:
In this post, I argue that individual intellectual activity can only be sustained in an intellectual community of other humans. AI dissolves these communities, which in turn makes private intellectual activity rarer.

Some years ago, when it became clear that AI would solve software engineering, my thinking was:

The second point has not quite worked out. What actually happened? First, the discourse of software engineering became worse. As I wrote earlier :

Claude Code was released a little over a year ago. In that short time, software engineering has been completely transformed. Materially, it might be positive: higher productivity, though at the cost of a messier codebase. Socially, it has been a disaster.

The discourse around software engineering has gotten dumber. It’s like everyone in the industry lost 30 IQ points. People used to talk about compilers, type systems, logic. Now they talk about “prompts”, “harnesses”, “loops”. The discourse is narrower, shallower, and more repetitive. There’s only so many times I can hear about “agentic harnesses” before I lose my mind.

Then there’s the loss of human capital formation: there is nothing to learn. Prompting is not a skill, at least, it’s a much shallower skill than software engineering. The instrumental dimension of the work has improved in that people can get more output per unit of effort, but the dimension of work that’s about building up human capital has collapsed. And maybe this is rational. Why learn to code at all? The computers can do that for us. And so the rigorous, systematic thinking you need to practice in order to be a good programmer: all gone. The machines can be rational for us. We can just vibe.

Second, contributing to the commons of software engineering is increasingly pointless. Before AI, you could publish open-source code, write blog posts to share ideas or inspire other people, write expository texts like tutorials, forum posts, textbooks etc. to teach people. After AI, what’s the point?

It’s not just “you can’t get GitHub stars or traffic to your blog”; rather, there is no sense of a common human project you can contribute to. There’s your own private garden of code, which you can grow infinitely in all directions with the help of AI, but you never have to leave the garden and go to the bazaar to trade with people. Under these conditions, it’s hard to care or do anything.

But does it actually matter? Does it matter if we stop writing blog posts about obscure JavaScript features, and designing new programming languages? Maybe writing code was always drudgery, and now we can move on to higher things, like math— oh, wait .

From observing what happened to software engineering, and what’s currently happening to mathematics, I think we can derive some general insights about intellectual practices in general.

We tend to think of intellectual activity as private and solitary: the philosopher sitting in his armchair, deriving the world ab initio . But intellectual activity has two inputs that can’t be acquired in isolation: a shared body of work to build upon, and motivation . The shared body of work is communal, unless you want to recapitulate the entire tech tree. Motivation we can break down into two components:

We tend to think of intrinsic motivation as the purest kind: endogenous, self-created, unmotivated by material or social gain. But it’s an emotion, and, like all emotions, it’s transient and short-lived. And this is rational: otherwise, we’d all be stuck in life-long unproductive obsessions. So, we need something to fill the gaps between moments of divine inspiration. Extrinsic motivation serves this function.

Private intellectual activity that is sustained, complex, and long-term requires an external intellectual community to provide material and motivation, like fuel and oxidizer. That private activity, in turn, sustains the community: by publishing papers, textbooks, code, etc., you add to the shared body of work for others to build on top of; by citing someone’s paper or contributing to their repository, you give them the recognition and honor that confirms they are doing useful work, which in turn motivates them to keep contributing.

Without community, you don’t get isolated individuals each working on their own things: you get nothing. The inputs to intellectual activity dry up: no one is adding to the shared body of work, and there are no peers to benefit from your own intellectual activity. Without this extrinsic motivation, you get less intellectual activity because, again, intrinsic motivation is fleeting.

After AI, intellectual contributions become unnecessary or redundant. In the case of software: the AIs write all the code, so what’s the point of writing either code or prose? The audience for those things is now severely diminished. Humans don’t write code anymore, so they won’t read blog posts about how to write code, or tutorials, or try new libraries or programming languages. In the case of mathematics: the AIs can prove theorems, write papers, explain papers, tutor students, and in the near future, they might write entire textbooks better than humans. So what’s the point of writing a paper, or a textbook? It’s superfluous.

If intellectual activity is unnecessary—if there’s no consequence to designing a new programming language or publishing a paper, or if there’s simply no community to contribute to—then it won’t happen. There’s no point.

Now apply this to every other domain of intellectual activity, and you see what the future looks like. There may be individuals building new libraries and programming languages, but no shared culture of software engineering; there may be individual students and practitioners of mathematics, but no living community of mathematicians.

I’ve spoken to people who think AI will have a positive effect on the life of the mind, and their thinking is that right now too many people are doing intellectual activity for instrumental reasons: citations, clout, etc. In this view, the collapse of intellectual communities is good , because it sifts the intrinsically-motivated übermenschen from the clout-chasing masses.

I think this view fits with contemporary society: we view intrinsic and extrinsic motivation as high and low status, respectively. A “developed” person is supposed to have a private, inexhaustible reserve of motivation which is causally disconnected from external reward.

But this is not a realistic view of human beings. Humans are social animals who can only flourish in the society of other humans. We care, and we should care, about contributing to the world. And if technology makes our contributions superfluous, then what is left?

Thanks to Luke Drago and Andy Matuschak for feedback and conversations.

items.title: RTX Spark, modelli, prezzi e disponibilità in Italia. Per Surface Laptop Ultra ci sarà da attendere
items.summary: I primi notebook con NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X si possono già configurare e ordinare in Italia: per la nuova piattaforma NVIDIA si parte da poco più di 3.000 euro e si arriva a oltre 6.000, con la differenza di prezzo legata quasi esclusivamente alla memoria. ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Sono aperti da meno di 24 ore i preordini dei primi laptop con piattaforma RTX Spark, e già arrivano le prime indicazioni: in Germania e in Francia, dove il Surface Laptop Ultra viene venduto, la versione da 128 GB di RAM è andata sold out in poche ore. Non possiamo ovviamente sapere di quanti laptop stiamo parlando, ma è evidente che da anni chi usa Windows aspettava una workstation con le caratteristiche promesse dal nuovo chip NVIDIA: consumi ridotti, piena potenza anche a batteria, fino a 128 GB di memoria unificata e prestazioni allineate a quelle della RTX 5070.

Il Surface Laptop Ultra in Italia al momento non arriva, e non escludiamo che la scelta possa essere legata proprio alla poca disponibilità di prodotto, ma MSI, Asus e Lenovo hanno aperto i preordini per i loro modelli, e la buona notizia è che si partirà da circa 3.000 euro, grazie a Lenovo, che offre una configurazione base molto allettante.

Lo Yoga Pro 9n Gen 11 da 15" parte infatti da 3.019,01 euro con N1X a 18 core (P-core fino a 3,90 GHz), 32 GB di LPDDR5X-9400 e 512 GB di storage. Se si vuole 1 TB di storage servono 90 euro in più.

Per avere più memoria bisogna passare alla versione da 20 core, con P-core fino a 4,00 GHz, che parte però da 4.839 euro con 64 GB di RAM e 1 TB di disco. Il disco da 2 TB costa 520 euro in più, si arriva a 5.339 euro. Stranamente basso il prezzo chiesto per passare alla versione da 128 GB: solo 300 euro, per un totale di 5.659 euro. È un prezzo alto, ma è anche il più basso in assoluto al quale si può trovare un RTX Spark con 128 GB di RAM.

Lenovo non ha solo il 15": c'è anche lo Yoga 9n 2-in-1 Gen 11 da 16", convertibile con OLED 2,8K (2.880 x 1.800) touch a 120 Hz e penna. Qui si parte da 3.619,01 euro per la versione con processore a 18 core, 32 GB di RAM e SSD da 512 GB. L'SSD da 1 TB costa qui 80 euro in più, mentre per il 20 core si passa a 4.759 euro, perché oltre al processore cambia anche la memoria, che sale a 64 GB. Il disco è da 1 TB, con 500 euro in più per il 2 TB. La memoria, invece, non si può espandere: questa macchina viene venduta solo nei tagli da 32 GB o da 64 GB.

MSI propone solo laptop con processore completo, quindi CPU a 20 core e GPU a 6.144 core. Il Prestige N16 Flip AI+, convertibile da 16" con batteria da 99,9 Wh e display Tandem OLED 3840 x 2400, parte da 4.299 euro per la versione da 64 GB con disco da 1 TB e arriva a 6.399 euro per quella da 128 GB con disco da 2 TB.

ASUS è l'unica a offrire RTX Spark in formato compatto, con il ProArt P14: 14" OLED 3K a 120 Hz, 1,48 kg e batteria da 90 Wh. I due modelli disponibili sono posizionati a 3.599 euro con 32 GB e a 5.599 euro con 128 GB, entrambi con la versione del processore più potente e con disco da 1 TB. C'è anche il modello da 16": 4.599 euro per 64 GB e 1 TB, 6.399 euro per il 128 GB con 2 TB.

Microsoft ha il bellissimo Surface Laptop Ultra, che possiamo considerare il reference design della piattaforma. In Italia non arriverà subito, ma possiamo prendere come riferimento i prezzi di Francia e Germania: 2.899 euro per RTX Spark in versione 18 core con GPU da 5.120 core, 24 GB e SSD da 512 GB; 3.399 euro per quella da 24 GB e 1 TB; 3.759 euro per 32 GB e 1 TB. La variante con processore completo, a 20 core e con GPU da 6.144 core, parte da 4.239 euro (32 GB, 1 TB), sale a 4.959 euro con 64 GB e a 5.439 euro con 2 TB, fino a 6.879 euro per la versione da 128 GB, che risulta, come abbiamo detto, già esaurita.

Al momento Dell e HP, gli altri due partner di NVIDIA per il lancio, non hanno annunciato la disponibilità per il nostro mercato.

items.title: Thai Queen makes first solo flight in fighter jet
items.summary: Thailand’s Queen Suthida made her first solo flight in a fighter jet, according to the Thai Royal Household.
items.content:
Thailand's Queen Suthida made her first solo flight in a fighter jet, according to the Thai Royal Household.

The Queen was shown boarding a Gripen on 8 October at an airfield in Surat Thani province, southern Thailand, while King Maha Vajiralongkorn watched from the ground.

The Royal Household has said she is an experienced pilot, having logged about 1,188 hours across several types of aircraft since she began flying in 2010.

She also co-piloted aircraft carrying the King on official visits to other countries, the Royal Household said.

items.title: Il tribunale rigetta il ricorso di Ranucci per il reintegro a Report. Il giornalista: "Rispetto la sentenza e la accetto serenamente"
items.summary: L'ex conduttore: "Le mie battaglie compensate dall'affetto della gente"
items.content:
A 14 giorni dall'udienza, il tribunale del Lavoro di Roma ha rigettato il ricorso in via urgente presentato dal giornalista Sigfrido Ranucci con cui chiedeva il reintegro alla conduzione della trasmissione Report dopo la decisione della Rai del 28 agosto scorso con cui era stato rimosso. L'azienda aveva offerto al giornalista tre opzioni : la vicedirezione al Tg3 o a Rainews, oppure l'ufficio di corrispondenza dal Cairo. Proposte respinte al mittente dall'ex conduttore e che è passato alla via giudiziaria per ottenere il reintegro. "Che io rispetti la decsione è ovvio: mi sono sempre battuto per l'indipendenza della magistratura e battersi per un valore del genere non significa togliersi la maglietta quando non ti fa comodo per poi rimetterla all'occorrenza", il commento a caldo di Ranucci.

Nel provvedimento di oltre 30 pagine i giudici ripercorrono la vicenda, citando anche l'episodio dell'attentato subito da Ranucci nell'ottobre del 2025 e affermando che la decisione della Rai "di procedere ad una riorganizzazione della redazione, con avvicendamento autorale e di conduzione, appare, a un esame sommario, sganciata dalla parallela vicenda disciplinare e adottata quale mezzo di risoluzione della situazione di tensione interna creatasi tra i membri della redazione e, come tale, strumento di tutela del sereno operare di questa nel rispetto della normativa di legge". Nell'ordinanza i giudici richiamano anche le argomentazioni difensive portate in giudizio dall'azienda pubblica. Per la Rai "l'individuazione del conduttore, e del gruppo autorale, di un determinato programma televisivo" rientra "nelle prerogative dell'impresa editoriale ed è insindacabile. Pertanto, il giornalista non è titolare di un diritto soggettivo ad occupare una determinata posizione nell'ambito della programmazione televisiva". Entrando nel merito della questione il tribunale afferma che "si deve ritenere accertato, quanto meno in questa fase e tenuto conto dei tempi ristretti imposti da un'istruttoria necessariamente sommaria, che, a conferma delle motivazioni pur genericamente espresse nel provvedimento" della Rai del 28 agosto, "le vicende legate al caso dell'attentato che man mano emergevano dagli articoli di giornale ed il clamore che queste suscitavano sugli organi di stampa, avevano creato nell'ambito della redazione un clima di tensione che incideva sul proficuo operare della stessa, tanto che diversi redattori avevano sentito la necessità di manifestare tale disagio non solo al responsabile del programma Ranucci ma anche, per saltum, al superiore gerarchico di quest'ultimo". E ancora: "il malessere manifestato da più giornalisti membri della redazione è stato confermato, seppur con diversi accenti, dal medesimo dottor Ranucci, parimenti sentito in udienza, il quale ha sul punto dichiarato: 'Si erano lamentati con me, anzi avevano fatto presente la necessità di sopportare insieme la pressione mediatica e puntellare la mia posizione tramite una riorganizzazione. Sentivano la pressione mediatica e quindi mi avevano coinvolto essendo loro responsabile. Avevano bisogno di puntellare Report intorno la mia persona perché per 20 anni avevo garantito l'esistenza del programma'". Su eventuali pressioni politiche messe in atto per ottenere dalla Rai lo stop alla conduzione, il tribunale afferma "che l'accertata impropria pressione mediatica esercitata ad opera di esponenti di rilievo della maggioranza di Governo sulle decisioni aziendali, volta all'adozione di un provvedimento di rimozione di Ranucci, quale unico dato indiziario non corroborato da altri, non offra in sé, tenuto conto del quadro complessivo degli elementi acquisiti, prova sufficiente a far ritenere che si sia consumata effettiva e determinante interferenza ".

Per Ranucci, "è una decisione che ha abbracciato l'idea secondo cui il clamore mediatico può arrivare a far sostituire un conduttore con una redazione che ha subito delle pressioni e che, di conseguenza, non vi sia la prova che i dirigenti Rai abbiano subito un'influenza diretta da parte della politica", sottolinea a margine dell'evento "Censura di Stato - A sostegno di Report e del giornalismo d'inchiesta", organizzato da ANTIMAFIADuemila a Roma, dove viene accolto tra gli applausi. "Tutte le battaglie che ho fatto nella mia vita e che mi hanno portato a 247 querele, a una bomba, a essere sospeso e a subire la decurtazione dello stipendio, trovano compenso solo nell'affetto della gente. L'avete visto tutti: per me significa che ho fatto bene e questo mi basta", aggiunge Ranucci. I legali del giornalista prendono "atto della decisione che rispettiamo ma che non condividiamo. Valuteremo il provvedimento e le ulteriori iniziative da assumere nelle sedi competenti", affermano in una nota gli avvocati Franco Focareta, Franco Scarpelli, Stefano Rossi e Roberto De Vita. Soddisfatta la Rai: "È importante riconoscere il lavoro svolto dai vertici aziendali nel rispetto delle procedure e delle proprie responsabilità. L'auspicio è che questa decisione contribuisca a ristabilire un clima di serenità", commenta la consigliera di amministrazione Rai Federica Frangi.

items.title: Madre e figlia morte avvelenate, disposta una perquisizione nella scuola delle sorelle Di Vita
items.summary: La polizia andrà anche nell'istituto dove insegna la professoressa amica dell'ex sindaco
items.content:
La prossima sarà una delle settimane più intense per l'inchiesta sul giallo della ricina in Molise. Gli investigatori, al lavoro da quasi dieci mesi sul caso delle due donne, mamma e figlia, morte a dicembre avvelenate con la ricina , saranno impegnati in tre giorni consecutivi di perquisizioni in altrettante scuole.

La procura di Larino ha deciso un'azione imponente per trovare il computer dal quale potrebbe essere stato cercato il veleno usato per uccidere Sara Di Vita, 15 anni, e sua mamma Antonella Di Ielsi, 50 anni. Si comincia martedì mattina dall'istituto Agrario di Riccia, dove lavora come tecnico di laboratorio il marito della professoressa amica di Gianni Di Vita, padre e marito delle vittime. Il giorno dopo, sempre a Riccia, gli uomini della Squadra Mobile e dello Sco si sposteranno al liceo scientifico, dove ha insegnato matematica la professoressa amica dell'ex sindaco. Giovedì, infine, nuova perquisizione a Campobasso, nel liceo Classico Mario Pagano, frequentato fino allo scorso anno scolastico da Sara e dalla sorella Alice. In tutto saranno ispezionati 155 computer: 71 all'istituto Agrario di Riccia, 63 al liceo Classico di Campobasso e 21 al liceo Scientifico di Riccia.

Le perquisizioni arrivano a pochi giorni da quelle effettuate a Pietracatella e Campobasso negli studi di lavoro e nella nuova abitazione di Gianni Di Vita. Questa nuova azione, però, si svolge come prova irripetibile: sono state quindi avvisate anche le parti, che potranno partecipare, tra cui indagati, avvocati, parti offese e consulenti. "Ispezione informatica": così la procuratrice di Larino Elvira Antonelli ha descritto l'operazione, che prevede anche l'eventuale sequestro dei pc. L'obiettivo è verificare se siano state effettuate ricerche sulla ricina, sulla provenienza del veleno usato per uccidere Sara e Antonella, sul suo eventuale acquisto online e sulle modalità di preparazione e somministrazione. Dalle indagini recenti sono già emerse navigazioni e ricerche sul web, effettuate da persone ancora sconosciute, proprio sulla ricina. La Squadra Mobile di Campobasso ha acquisito nei mesi scorsi i dati dei dispositivi informatici presenti negli istituti frequentati da persone che hanno avuto rapporti con le vittime. "Non può escludersi - scrive la procuratrice - che con gli stessi siano state eseguite navigazioni nel web/dark web afferenti alle parole 'ricina', 'veleno' e simili". Tra i termini attenzionati dagli investigatori figurano anche 'solfato di ammonio', 'solfato di sodio', 'esano', 'ricino', 'semi di ricino', 'olio di ricino', 'deep web' e 'dark web'. Nel disporre le perquisizioni, la procuratrice ha precisato che l'accertamento non può limitarsi alla presenza di determinate parole nei file visibili, ma dovrà eventualmente comprendere "l'analisi degli artefatti digitali idonei a ricostruire l'effettiva attività di navigazione, ricerca, consultazione, download, creazione, modifica o cancellazione di contenuti pertinenti ai fatti per cui si procede". Alla polizia è stato chiesto anche di verificare "l'eventuale utilizzo di strumenti destinati alla navigazione anonima". "Assume particolare rilievo investigativo - conclude la procuratrice - anche, dove tecnicamente possibile, la collocazione temporale delle ricerche e la persona concretamente utilizzatrice del dispositivo", soprattutto considerando il possibile uso condiviso dei computer nelle scuole. L'inchiesta sul caso di Pietracatella è ancora contro ignoti per l'ipotesi di duplice omicidio premeditato, mentre cinque medici sono indagati per omicidio colposo in relazione ai soccorsi prestati alle vittime dopo i malori.
